questions.explanation: The pneumotaxic center, located in the pons, regulates the duration of inspiration and prevents excessive lung expansion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the conducting part of the respiratory system?
questions.explanation: The conducting part of the respiratory system transports air, filters it, and humidifies it, but gas exchange occurs only in the alveoli.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors does not influence breathing rate?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is not involved in the regulation of breathing rate, unlike CO₂, O₂, and blood pH.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has the highest solubility in blood?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is 20-25 times more soluble in blood than oxygen, making it easier to transport.

questions.question_text: Which part of the respiratory system is responsible for warming and filtering inhaled air?
questions.explanation: The nasal chamber warms, filters, and humidifies inhaled air before it reaches the lungs.

questions.question_text: Which lung volume represents the additional amount of air that can be inhaled after a normal inspiration?
questions.explanation: Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) is the additional amount of air a person can inhale after a normal inspiration.

questions.question_text: Which neural center primarily regulates respiratory rhythm?
questions.explanation: The respiratory rhythm center in the medulla oblongata controls the basic rhythm of breathing.

tests.title: Breathing and Exchange of Gases Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: Which part of the respiratory system is commonly called the "voice box"?
questions.explanation: The larynx is known as the voice box because it contains the vocal cords responsible for sound production.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about lung function is correct?
options: Lung expansion is caused by contraction of the pleura.
Air moves into the lungs when intrapulmonary pressure is lower than atmospheric pressure.
Gas exchange occurs primarily in the bronchi.
Expiration is caused by contraction of the diaphragm.
questions.explanation: Inhalation occurs when intrapulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric pressure, allowing air to flow into the lungs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly represents the partial pressure of oxygen (pO₂) in the alveoli?
questions.explanation: The partial pressure of oxygen (pO₂) in the alveoli is approximately 104 mmHg, facilitating its diffusion into the blood.

questions.question_text: What is the function of surfactant in the alveoli?
questions.explanation: Surfactant is a lipoprotein that reduces surface tension in the alveoli, preventing their collapse during exhalation.

questions.question_text: Which parameter is used to assess lung function in a clinical setting?
questions.explanation: Spirometry is a clinical tool used to assess lung function by measuring various respiratory volumes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about hemoglobin and oxygen transport is correct?
options: Oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin is influenced by pH and pCO₂ levels.
Oxygen transport is unaffected by temperature changes.
Oxygen binds to hemoglobin in tissues and is released in the lungs.
questions.explanation: Oxygen dissociation from hemoglobin is influenced by factors such as pH, pCO₂ levels, and temperature, known as the **Bohr effect**.

questions.question_text: What type of respiration is used by amphibians like frogs in addition to pulmonary respiration?
questions.explanation: Amphibians like frogs use cutaneous respiration, where gas exchange occurs through their moist skin in addition to lungs.

questions.question_text: Which part of the respiratory system is the common passage for food and air?
questions.explanation: The pharynx serves as a common passage for both air (to the lungs) and food (to the esophagus).

questions.question_text: Which of the following animals use tracheal tubes for respiration?
questions.explanation: Insects use a network of tracheal tubes to transport atmospheric air within their body for respiration.

questions.question_text: Which lung capacity includes Tidal Volume and Inspiratory Reserve Volume?
questions.explanation: Inspiratory Capacity (IC) includes Tidal Volume (TV) and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV), representing the maximum volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Test 1

questions.question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is responsible for DNA replication?
questions.explanation: The S phase (Synthesis phase) is the stage where DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes anaphase I of meiosis from anaphase of mitosis?
options: Sister chromatids separate in meiosis but not in mitosis
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis but not in mitosis
DNA replication occurs in anaphase I
Centromeres do not split in mitosis
questions.explanation: In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitosis, sister chromatids separate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following events occurs during anaphase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number by half.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about anaphase is correct?
options: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cytokinesis is correct?
options: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow
Plant cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow
Cytokinesis does not occur in mitosis
questions.explanation: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by forming a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells, a cell plate forms instead.

questions.question_text: Which of the following events occurs in anaphase?
options: Chromosomes align at the center of the cell
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.

questions.question_text: Which phase of mitosis directly follows metaphase?
questions.explanation: Anaphase follows metaphase, during which sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.

questions.question_text: Which checkpoint ensures proper chromosome alignment before anaphase begins?
questions.explanation: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned at the metaphase plate before anaphase begins.

questions.question_text: What is the outcome of meiosis II?
questions.explanation: Meiosis II results in four haploid daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following happens during pachytene of meiosis I?
questions.explanation: During pachytene, homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material through crossing over.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Test 2

questions.question_text: Which structure is responsible for chromosome movement during cell division?
questions.explanation: Spindle fibers, composed of microtubules, attach to kinetochores on chromosomes and facilitate their movement.

questions.question_text: Which phase of interphase is characterized by intense metabolic activity and cell growth?
questions.explanation: The G1 phase is the period between mitosis and DNA replication, characterized by active metabolism and cell growth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?
options: It occurs only in haploid cells
It results in genetically identical daughter cells
It reduces the chromosome number by half
It occurs only in reproductive cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, maintaining the chromosome number of the parent cell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about G0 phase is correct?
options: Cells in G0 phase cannot divide again
Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive
Cells in G0 phase can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions
G0 phase is a part of mitosis
questions.explanation: Cells in G0 phase are metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when needed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the G1 phase is incorrect?
options: It is the first phase of interphase
Cell growth and metabolism occur in this phase
DNA replication occurs in this phase
questions.explanation: DNA replication does not occur in G1; it takes place in the S phase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?
options: Mitosis occurs in both somatic and germ cells
Mitosis produces two diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is correct?
questions.explanation: During telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around each set of chromosomes, which decondense.

questions.question_text: Which of the following phases is also known as the “resting phase” of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: The G0 phase is a quiescent phase where cells temporarily or permanently exit the cell cycle.

questions.question_text: Which structure helps separate chromosomes during mitosis?
questions.explanation: Spindle fibers attach to chromosomes via kinetochores and help pull them apart during mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is correct?
options: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases
Mitosis is the longest phase of the cell cycle
DNA replication occurs in the G2 phase
Cell division does not occur in prokaryotes
questions.explanation: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases, where the cell prepares for division. Mitosis is not the longest phase, and DNA replication occurs in the S phase.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Test 3

questions.question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the "resting phase"?
questions.explanation: The G0 phase is a quiescent stage where cells do not divide but remain metabolically active.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent phase (G0) is correct?
options: Cells in G0 never re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase is a metabolically inactive state
Cells can re-enter the cell cycle when required
G0 phase is the shortest phase in the cell cycle
questions.explanation: Cells in G0 remain metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when stimulated by external signals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during telophase I of meiosis?
questions.explanation: During telophase I, homologous chromosomes reach opposite poles, and nuclear membranes may reappear.

questions.question_text: What is the function of the centrioles during mitosis?
questions.explanation: Centrioles help in forming spindle fibers that assist in the movement of chromosomes during mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about diplotene is correct?
questions.explanation: During diplotene, chiasmata (points of crossing over) become visible as homologous chromosomes start separating.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?
options: Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number
Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the chromosome number further.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about cytokinesis?
options: Animal cells undergo cytokinesis by forming a cell plate
Cytokinesis ensures equal distribution of cytoplasm
Cytokinesis differs between plant and animal cells
questions.explanation: Animal cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow, whereas plant cells form a cell plate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following phases is the longest in the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: G1 phase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, where cells grow and prepare for DNA replication.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a function of mitosis?
options: Repair and replacement of damaged cells
questions.explanation: Gamete formation occurs through meiosis, not mitosis. Mitosis is responsible for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase of mitosis?
options: Chromosomes are aligned at the equator
questions.explanation: During prophase, chromosomes condense, the nuclear membrane breaks down, and spindle fibers form, but chromosome alignment occurs in metaphase.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Test 4

questions.question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest in a typical eukaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Interphase occupies more than 95% of the cell cycle and includes G1, S, and G2 phases.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of meiosis in sexually reproducing organisms?
options: It reduces the chromosome number to half, ensuring genetic diversity
It produces identical cells for growth and repair
It only helps in asexual reproduction
questions.explanation: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half and ensures genetic variation in sexually reproducing organisms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following events occurs during prophase I of meiosis but not in prophase of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis, leading to genetic recombination, whereas it does not occur in mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the metaphase plate?
options: Region where spindle fibers are synthesized
Plane where chromosomes align during metaphase
Structure that holds sister chromatids together
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, an imaginary plane equidistant from the spindle poles.

questions.question_text: What happens during the diplotene stage of prophase I?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: During diplotene, homologous chromosomes start separating as the synaptonemal complex dissolves, but remain attached at chiasmata.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about anaphase I of meiosis?
options: Homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) separate and move to opposite poles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is incorrect?
options: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle
M phase includes mitosis and cytokinesis
G1 phase occurs after the S phase
S phase is responsible for DNA replication
questions.explanation: G1 phase occurs before the S phase, not after it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about interphase is incorrect?
options: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases
Interphase is the shortest phase of the cell cycle
DNA replication occurs in the S phase of interphase
Interphase prepares the cell for mitosis
questions.explanation: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, not the shortest.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G1 phase?
options: The cell grows in size during G1 phase
Organelles are duplicated in G1 phase
DNA replication occurs in G1 phase
Cells prepare for DNA synthesis in G1 phase
questions.explanation: DNA replication does not occur in G1 phase; it happens in the S phase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about the M checkpoint?
options: It ensures that DNA replication is complete
It occurs at the end of G1 phase
It ensures that all chromosomes are attached to spindle fibers before anaphase
questions.explanation: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle fibers before anaphase begins.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about anaphase?
options: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and are pulled toward opposite poles by spindle fibers.

questions.question_text: Which phase of mitosis immediately follows metaphase?
questions.explanation: Anaphase follows metaphase, where sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is incorrect?
questions.explanation: During telophase, sister chromatids have already separated in anaphase; they do not remain attached.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the S phase of interphase?
options: DNA replication occurs, doubling the chromosome number
The cell grows and prepares for mitosis
questions.explanation: During the S phase, DNA is replicated, doubling the chromosome content of the cell but not the chromosome number.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a cell type that remains in the G0 phase permanently?
questions.explanation: Nerve cells enter G0 phase permanently and do not divide after differentiation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?
options: Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number
Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the chromosome number further.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent (G0) phase is correct?
options: Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive
Nerve and heart cells enter G0 permanently
Cells in G0 phase cannot re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase occurs after mitosis and before cytokinesis
questions.explanation: Nerve and heart cells remain in G0 permanently, while some other cells may re-enter the cycle under specific conditions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures plays a crucial role in cytokinesis of plant cells?
questions.explanation: In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs via the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a new cell wall.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the centromere?
options: It is the region where sister chromatids are attached
Spindle fibers attach to the centromere during cell division
It helps in the separation of homologous chromosomes in meiosis
questions.explanation: The centromere remains intact during metaphase and serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about interphase is incorrect?
options: Interphase is also called the resting phase
DNA replication occurs in the S phase of interphase
G1 phase follows the S phase
G2 phase prepares the cell for mitosis
questions.explanation: G1 phase comes before the S phase, not after it.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs at the end of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Meiosis results in the formation of four genetically distinct haploid cells.

questions.question_text: During which phase of mitosis does chromatin condense into visible chromosomes?
questions.explanation: During prophase, chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes, making them visible under a microscope.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is incorrect?
options: Meiosis results in four haploid cells
Meiosis is a type of asexual reproduction
questions.explanation: Meiosis is a type of sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction.

questions.question_text: What is the role of kinetochores during cell division?
options: Act as sites of spindle fiber attachment
questions.explanation: Kinetochores are protein structures on the centromere where spindle fibers attach to move chromosomes.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of meiosis II?
options: To reduce chromosome number by half
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis and is responsible for the separation of sister chromatids into different cells.

questions.question_text: How does meiosis contribute to genetic variation?
options: By ensuring identical copies of DNA are passed to daughter cells
Through crossing over and independent assortment
Through DNA replication in meiosis II
questions.explanation: Meiosis introduces genetic variation through crossing over during prophase I and independent assortment during metaphase I.

questions.question_text: What is the role of kinetochores during cell division?
options: They help in chromosome movement by attaching to spindle fibers
questions.explanation: Kinetochores are protein structures at the centromere that facilitate chromosome movement by attaching to spindle fibers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of telophase in mitosis?
questions.explanation: Centromeres divide in anaphase, not telophase. In telophase, chromosomes decondense and the nuclear membrane reforms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase I of meiosis?
options: Homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids remain together.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about chromatin and chromosomes is correct?
options: Chromatin is the condensed form of chromosomes
Chromosomes exist only during cell division
Chromatin is composed of DNA and proteins
questions.explanation: Chromatin consists of DNA and proteins (mainly histones) and condenses into chromosomes during cell division.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: At which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align at the center of the cell?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, preparing for equal distribution to daughter cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is correct?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: During telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which phase of meiosis is responsible for the formation of chiasmata?
questions.explanation: During diplotene, homologous chromosomes begin to separate except at chiasmata, where crossing over has occurred.

questions.question_text: What is the function of recombinase enzyme in meiosis?
questions.explanation: Recombinase is an enzyme that facilitates crossing over during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cell division checkpoints is correct?
options: G1 checkpoint ensures DNA has replicated correctly
M checkpoint ensures chromosomes are aligned properly
G2 checkpoint occurs before DNA replication
questions.explanation: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned before proceeding to anaphase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?
options: Meiosis II is identical to mitosis
Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number
DNA replication occurs before meiosis II
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis, as it involves the separation of sister chromatids without further reduction in chromosome number.

questions.question_text: Which structure disappears during prophase of mitosis?
questions.explanation: During prophase, the nuclear envelope disintegrates, allowing spindle fibers to attach to chromosomes.

questions.question_text: What is the end result of meiosis in terms of chromosome number?
questions.explanation: Meiosis results in haploid cells, ensuring that gametes have half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase I of meiosis?
options: It is longer and more complex than prophase of mitosis
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs in the pachytene stage, not in zygotene.

questions.question_text: What is a key difference between meiosis I and meiosis II?
options: DNA replication occurs in meiosis I but not in meiosis II
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis II, not in meiosis I
Meiosis I produces haploid cells, while meiosis II produces diploid cells
Cytokinesis occurs only in meiosis I
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs only in meiosis I during the S phase, not in meiosis II, which is similar to mitosis.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: Which event is unique to meiosis and does not occur in mitosis?
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis and is responsible for genetic recombination.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the centromere during cell division?
questions.explanation: The centromere serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers, ensuring proper chromosome movement during division.

questions.question_text: Which type of cell division occurs in the apical and lateral meristem of plants?
questions.explanation: Mitosis occurs in the apical and lateral meristem, leading to the continuous growth of plants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is correct?
options: Meiosis occurs in both diploid and haploid cells
Meiosis involves two rounds of cell division
Meiosis results in the production of diploid cells
Meiosis does not contribute to genetic variation
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two divisions (meiosis I and II) and produces haploid cells, contributing to genetic variation.

questions.question_text: Which event marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in mitosis?
questions.explanation: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about prophase is incorrect?
questions.explanation: During prophase, the nuclear envelope breaks down, allowing the spindle fibers to interact with chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about G2 phase?
options: G2 phase occurs before the S phase
The cell checks for DNA replication errors in G2 phase
G2 phase is longer than G1 phase
DNA replication takes place in G2 phase
questions.explanation: The G2 phase is a checkpoint where the cell ensures that DNA replication was completed correctly before mitosis begins.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about metaphase is incorrect?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
Sister chromatids move to opposite poles
Metaphase is the best stage to study chromosome morphology
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids move to opposite poles in anaphase.

questions.question_text: During which phase of mitosis do spindle fibers attach to kinetochores?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and align the chromosomes at the equatorial plate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about genetic variation in meiosis?
options: Crossing over occurs during prophase I
Independent assortment occurs during metaphase I
Meiosis results in genetically identical cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces genetically varied cells due to crossing over and independent assortment, not identical ones.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 9

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?
options: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half
Meiosis consists of one round of division
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II), not just one.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase II of meiosis?
questions.explanation: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, similar to anaphase of mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is incorrect?
options: Mitosis results in two genetically identical daughter cells
Mitosis is essential for growth and repair
questions.explanation: Crossing over does not occur in mitosis; it occurs during prophase I of meiosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about G2 phase?
options: Proteins necessary for mitosis are synthesized
DNA replication occurs in this phase
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs in the S phase, not in G2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
Metaphase is an important stage for karyotyping
questions.explanation: Sister chromatids do not separate in metaphase; they separate during anaphase.

questions.question_text: Which event distinguishes meiosis I from mitosis?
options: Homologous chromosomes pair and undergo recombination
questions.explanation: During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes pair up and undergo recombination, which does not occur in mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which phase of meiosis involves the separation of sister chromatids?
questions.explanation: During anaphase II, the sister chromatids of each chromosome separate and move toward opposite poles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase I of meiosis?
options: It is longer than prophase of mitosis
Chromosomes do not condense in prophase I
questions.explanation: Chromosomes condense during prophase I of meiosis.

questions.question_text: What is the main feature of metaphase I of meiosis?
options: Chromosomes align at the equator as bivalents
Chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: In metaphase I, bivalents (paired homologous chromosomes) align at the metaphase plate.

questions.question_text: What is the function of spindle fibers during cell division?
questions.explanation: Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and help in the movement and separation of chromatids or homologous chromosomes during cell division.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 10

questions.question_text: What happens to the chromosome number during meiosis I?
questions.explanation: During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number from diploid to haploid.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase I but not in mitotic anaphase?
questions.explanation: During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids separate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about prophase is correct?
questions.explanation: During prophase, centrosomes migrate to opposite poles to form the mitotic spindle.

questions.question_text: Which event occurs in anaphase II but not in anaphase I?
questions.explanation: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, whereas in anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about crossing over in meiosis?
options: Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I
It involves exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes
Crossing over leads to genetic recombination
Crossing over occurs during metaphase II
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I, not in metaphase II.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?
options: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half
Meiosis consists of one round of division
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II), not just one.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase I of meiosis is incorrect?
options: DNA replication occurs before meiosis II
questions.explanation: There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis produces haploid cells, meiosis produces diploid cells
Mitosis occurs in gametes, meiosis occurs in somatic cells
Mitosis produces identical cells, meiosis results in genetic variation
Mitosis involves two cell divisions, meiosis involves one
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, while meiosis introduces genetic variation through recombination.

questions.question_text: Which stage of mitosis is best for studying chromosome morphology?
questions.explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes are fully condensed and aligned at the equatorial plate, making them ideal for studying morphology.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G0 phase?
options: G0 is a resting phase where cells do not divide
Nerve and muscle cells remain in G0 permanently
All cells in G0 phase can never re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase occurs after the G1 phase
questions.explanation: Some cells in G0 can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 11

questions.question_text: Which of the following events occurs during zygotene of prophase I?
questions.explanation: During zygotene, homologous chromosomes pair up in a process called synapsis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about metaphase is incorrect?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
Metaphase is the stage where chromosomes are most condensed
questions.explanation: During metaphase, the nuclear membrane remains absent; it reforms during telophase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following events occurs during telophase II of meiosis?
questions.explanation: During telophase II, the nuclear membrane reforms around the newly separated chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during zygotene of prophase I?
options: Chromosomes start pairing to form bivalents
questions.explanation: During zygotene, homologous chromosomes start pairing, a process called synapsis, forming bivalents.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between cytokinesis in plant and animal cells?
options: Plant cells divide by furrowing, while animal cells form a cell plate
Animal cells divide by furrowing, while plant cells form a cell plate
Both plant and animal cells use the same mechanism
Animal cells use microtubules, while plant cells do not
questions.explanation: Animal cells divide through cleavage furrow formation, while plant cells form a cell plate during cytokinesis.

questions.question_text: How does mitosis differ from meiosis?
options: Mitosis produces four cells, while meiosis produces two
Mitosis results in haploid cells, while meiosis results in diploid cells
Mitosis maintains chromosome number, while meiosis reduces it
Mitosis involves two rounds of division, while meiosis has one
questions.explanation: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number, while meiosis reduces it by half, ensuring haploid gamete formation.

questions.question_text: Which checkpoint ensures that DNA replication is complete before mitosis begins?
questions.explanation: The G2 checkpoint ensures that DNA replication is complete and checks for errors before the cell enters mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cytokinesis is correct?
options: Cytokinesis is the same in both plant and animal cells
Cytokinesis is not required for cell division
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis occurs after nuclear division and differs between plant and animal cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis I?
options: It reduces the chromosome number by half
It includes prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase
questions.explanation: Meiosis I produces haploid daughter cells, not diploid.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during the S phase of interphase?
options: Chromosomes align at the equatorial plate
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs in the S phase, ensuring each daughter cell receives an identical set of genetic material.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 12

questions.question_text: What happens during cytokinesis in an animal cell?
questions.explanation: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a cleavage furrow, which deepens to divide the cell into two.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase I but not in anaphase of mitosis?
questions.explanation: During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, while in mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids separate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?
options: Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number
Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the chromosome number further.

questions.question_text: What marks the transition from metaphase to anaphase in mitosis?
questions.explanation: During the transition from metaphase to anaphase, sister chromatids separate and begin moving to opposite poles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct about interkinesis?
options: Interkinesis is a resting phase between meiosis I and II
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: Interkinesis is a short resting phase between meiosis I and II, but no DNA replication occurs.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is essential for growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction by producing identical cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about telophase I of meiosis?
options: DNA replication occurs before meiosis II
questions.explanation: There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.

questions.question_text: Which stage of meiosis involves crossing over?
questions.explanation: During Prophase I, homologous chromosomes undergo crossing over, increasing genetic diversity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase II is incorrect?
options: Nuclear membrane reforms around each set of chromosomes
Four haploid daughter cells are produced
questions.explanation: During telophase II, chromosomes decondense, and nuclear membranes reform.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about metaphase I is incorrect?
options: Homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, but sister chromatids remain together.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 13

questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT occur in interphase?
questions.explanation: Chromosome segregation occurs during mitosis, whereas interphase is mainly for growth, DNA replication, and preparation for division.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about G2 phase is correct?
options: Cell growth and protein synthesis occur in G2 phase
DNA replication takes place in G2 phase
G2 phase is shorter than M phase
questions.explanation: During G2 phase, the cell prepares for mitosis by growing and synthesizing proteins required for division.

questions.question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the "synthesis phase"?
questions.explanation: The S phase (synthesis phase) is when DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material in preparation for cell division.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about telophase II?
questions.explanation: Telophase II results in four haploid cells, not diploid cells.

questions.question_text: What is the key feature of diplotene in meiosis I?
options: Separation of homologous chromosomes except at chiasmata
questions.explanation: In diplotene, homologous chromosomes start separating but remain attached at chiasmata where crossing over occurred.

questions.question_text: During which phase of meiosis does synapsis occur?
questions.explanation: Synapsis occurs during zygotene, where homologous chromosomes pair up and form synaptonemal complexes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about metaphase is incorrect?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
Metaphase is the best stage to study chromosome morphology
questions.explanation: During metaphase, the nuclear membrane remains absent; it reforms during telophase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?
options: Meiosis I and II both include prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase
DNA replication occurs between meiosis I and II
Meiosis results in four haploid cells
questions.explanation: DNA replication does not occur between meiosis I and II.

questions.question_text: Which phase in the cell cycle follows DNA replication?
questions.explanation: G2 phase follows the S phase and involves the synthesis of proteins required for mitosis.

questions.question_text: Which stage of meiosis ensures the reduction of chromosome number?
questions.explanation: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number by half.

tests.title: Cell Cycle And Cell Division Chapter-Wise Test 14

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes cytokinesis in animal cells?
options: Spindle fibers push daughter cells apart
questions.explanation: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two daughter cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about cytokinesis is correct?
options: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow
Plant cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow
Cytokinesis does not occur in mitosis
questions.explanation: Animal cells undergo cytokinesis through a cleavage furrow, while plant cells form a cell plate.

questions.question_text: What is the significance of the centromere in mitosis?
options: It is the site where spindle fibers attach to chromosomes
It controls the progression of the cell cycle
questions.explanation: The centromere is the region where spindle fibers attach during cell division to facilitate chromosome movement.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs only in meiosis and not in mitosis?
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosome pairing occurs only in meiosis during prophase I, leading to genetic recombination.

questions.question_text: What happens during interkinesis?
questions.explanation: Interkinesis is the resting phase between meiosis I and meiosis II, during which no DNA replication occurs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about genetic variation in meiosis is incorrect?
options: Crossing over occurs during prophase I
Independent assortment occurs during metaphase I
Meiosis results in genetically identical cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces genetically varied cells due to crossing over and independent assortment, not identical ones.

questions.question_text: What is the main event during anaphase of mitosis?
options: Chromosomes align at the equatorial plate
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
questions.explanation: During anaphase, the centromeres split, and sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles by spindle fibers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about prophase is correct?
options: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate
questions.explanation: During prophase, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, and spindle fibers begin to form.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis I and meiosis II is incorrect?
options: Meiosis I reduces the chromosome number by half
DNA replication occurs before both meiosis I and II
Meiosis results in four haploid cells
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs only before meiosis I, not between meiosis I and II.

questions.question_text: Which checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle fibers before progressing?
questions.explanation: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are correctly attached to spindle fibers before progressing to anaphase.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life' For NEET Test 1

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the principal function of the Golgi apparatus?
options: It packages materials for delivery within the cell or secretion outside the cell.
It synthesises proteins directly from amino acids.
It produces ATP during aerobic respiration.
It stores the genetic material of the cell.
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages materials received from the endoplasmic reticulum. These materials are then delivered to intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell.

questions.question_text: Which property of the plasma membrane enables it to regulate the movement of substances across the cell boundary?
options: It is composed entirely of proteins.
It is completely impermeable to polar molecules.
It contains a rigid layer of cellulose.
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain molecules or ions to move across it. Substances may cross by passive transport, facilitated transport or active transport.

questions.question_text: Which combination correctly represents the constituents of chromatin?
options: DNA, histones, non-histone proteins and RNA
questions.explanation: Chromatin contains DNA, basic proteins called histones, non-histone proteins and RNA. During cell division, the chromatin material becomes organised into distinct chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes nuclear pores?
options: They are sites of ATP synthesis within the nucleus.
They connect the nucleolus directly with the Golgi apparatus.
They are formed only in prokaryotic cells.
They permit the movement of RNA and proteins between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: Nuclear pores are formed where the two membranes of the nuclear envelope fuse. RNA and protein molecules move through these pores in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

questions.question_text: Which cellular structure is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane-bound structures composed of RNA and proteins. They serve as the sites of protein synthesis in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

questions.question_text: Which cellular structure is extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus?
questions.explanation: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus. Its outer surface bears ribosomes and it is commonly found in cells involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

questions.question_text: What is the main component of the middle lamella in plant cells?
questions.explanation: The middle lamella is composed mainly of calcium pectate. It holds or glues neighbouring plant cells together.

questions.question_text: Who first saw and described a live cell?
questions.explanation: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus, while Schleiden and Virchow contributed to the development of cell theory.

questions.question_text: Which statement is inconsistent with the cell theory as understood today?
options: New cells arise spontaneously from non-living material.
All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
Schleiden and Schwann together formulated the cell theory.
questions.explanation: The idea that new cells arise spontaneously from non-living material is inconsistent with cell theory. Rudolf Virchow explained that cells divide and new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the nucleolus is incorrect?
options: It is present within the nucleoplasm.
It is surrounded by a membrane.
It is a site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
It may be larger and more numerous in cells actively synthesising proteins.
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is not surrounded by a membrane. It is a spherical structure within the nucleoplasm and is a site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life' For NEET Test 2

questions.question_text: Which sequence correctly represents the layers of a typical bacterial cell envelope from the outermost to the innermost side?
questions.explanation: The bacterial cell envelope is a tightly bound three-layered structure. Its outermost layer is the glycocalyx, followed by the cell wall and then the plasma membrane.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes bacterial fimbriae from bacterial flagella?
options: Fimbriae may help bacteria attach to surfaces, whereas flagella are associated with motility.
Fimbriae contain the bacterial chromosome, whereas flagella contain plasmids.
Fimbriae synthesise proteins, whereas flagella synthesise lipids.
Fimbriae are membrane-bound organelles, whereas flagella are inclusion bodies.
questions.explanation: Fimbriae are small bristle-like surface structures that may help bacteria attach to rocks or host tissues. Bacterial flagella are filamentous extensions associated with motility.

questions.question_text: Which combination correctly describes inclusion bodies in prokaryotic cells?
options: Membrane-bound structures involved in intracellular digestion
Infoldings of the plasma membrane involved in respiration
Tubular structures involved in bacterial attachment
Non-membrane-bound structures that store reserve materials in the cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Inclusion bodies store reserve materials in prokaryotic cells. They are not surrounded by a membrane and lie freely in the cytoplasm; examples include phosphate, cyanophycean and glycogen granules.

questions.question_text: A substance is transported across the plasma membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration. Which statement best describes this process?
options: It is osmosis and involves only the movement of water.
It is active transport and requires energy supplied through ATP.
It is simple diffusion and does not require energy.
It is passive transport occurring along the concentration gradient.
questions.explanation: Movement against a concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration, is active transport. It is an energy-dependent process in which ATP is utilised; the Na + /K + pump is an example.

questions.question_text: What is the structural significance of cristae in a mitochondrion?
options: They increase the surface area of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
They enclose the mitochondrial DNA within a nuclear membrane.
They connect neighbouring mitochondria through cytoplasmic channels.
They form the continuous outer boundary of the mitochondrion.
questions.explanation: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane that project towards the matrix. These infoldings increase the surface area of the inner membrane.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly matches a type of leucoplast with the material it stores?
questions.explanation: Aleuroplasts are colourless plastids that store proteins. Amyloplasts store carbohydrates such as starch, whereas elaioplasts store oils and fats.

questions.question_text: Which chloroplast structure connects the thylakoids of different grana?
questions.explanation: Stroma lamellae are flat membranous tubules that connect the thylakoids of different grana. Grana are stacks of thylakoids located within the chloroplast stroma.

questions.question_text: Which arrangement of microtubules is usually present in the axoneme of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum?
options: Nine peripheral triplets without central microtubules
Eight peripheral doublets and two central microtubules
Nine peripheral singlets and one central microtubule
Nine peripheral doublets and two central microtubules
questions.explanation: The axoneme usually contains nine radially arranged peripheral microtubule doublets and a pair of centrally located microtubules. This organisation is called the 9+2 array.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the arrangement of centrioles in a centrosome?
options: The two centrioles lie parallel to each other and contain nine peripheral doublets.
The two centrioles lie perpendicular to each other and each has a cartwheel-like organisation.
A centrosome contains a single centriole surrounded by a membrane.
The centrioles are joined end to end and contain a central pair of microtubules.
questions.explanation: A centrosome usually contains two cylindrical centrioles lying perpendicular to each other. Each centriole has a cartwheel-like organisation with nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not listed as a function of mesosomes in prokaryotic cells?
options: Helping in DNA replication and its distribution to daughter cells
Increasing the surface area and enzymatic content of the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are plasma-membrane infoldings associated with cell-wall formation, DNA replication and distribution, respiration, secretion, and increased membrane surface area. Protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes, not on mesosomes.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life' For NEET Test 3

questions.question_text: Which observation best illustrates the relationship between the shape of a cell and the function it performs?
options: All cells of a multicellular organism have the same shape.
A cell retains one fixed shape regardless of its activity.
Cells differ only in size, while their shapes remain identical.
Cells may be disc-like, columnar, thread-like or irregular according to their functions.
questions.explanation: Cells vary greatly in shape and may be disc-like, polygonal, columnar, cuboid, thread-like or irregular. Their shape may vary according to the function they perform.

questions.question_text: A bacterium possesses a small circular DNA molecule in addition to its genomic DNA. Which conclusion is correct?
options: It is a plasmid that may confer a characteristic such as antibiotic resistance.
It is a nucleolus responsible for ribosomal RNA synthesis.
It is a lysosome containing hydrolytic enzymes.
It is a chromosome enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules present outside the genomic DNA in many bacteria. They may confer distinctive phenotypic characters, such as resistance to antibiotics.

questions.question_text: On what basis are bacteria classified as Gram-positive or Gram-negative?
options: The number and arrangement of their flagella
Differences in their cell envelopes and their response to Gram staining
The presence or absence of plasmid DNA
The shape and size of their ribosomes
questions.explanation: Bacteria are classified according to differences in their cell envelopes and their response to the Gram staining procedure. Those that take up the stain are Gram-positive; the others are Gram-negative.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly distinguishes the two forms of bacterial glycocalyx?
options: The slime layer is thick and tough, whereas the capsule is loose.
The slime layer contains ribosomes, whereas the capsule contains DNA.
The slime layer is a loose sheath, whereas the capsule is thick and tough.
The slime layer is the plasma membrane, whereas the capsule is the cell wall.
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx varies in composition and thickness. In some bacteria it occurs as a loose sheath called the slime layer, while in others it forms a thick and tough capsule.

questions.question_text: Which structure contains pigments in prokaryotes such as cyanobacteria?
questions.explanation: Chromatophores are membranous extensions into the cytoplasm of some prokaryotes, such as cyanobacteria. These structures contain pigments.

questions.question_text: Several ribosomes attached to a single messenger RNA form a chain. What is this arrangement called?
questions.explanation: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA to form a polyribosome or polysome. The ribosomes of the polysome translate the mRNA into protein.

questions.question_text: Which group contains only components of the endomembrane system?
options: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles
Endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, chloroplasts and lysosomes
Golgi apparatus, ribosomes, peroxisomes and vacuoles
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are excluded.

questions.question_text: Why may the concentration of certain ions be significantly higher inside a plant vacuole than in the cytoplasm?
options: The vacuole synthesises ions from water.
The tonoplast facilitates their transport into the vacuole against concentration gradients.
The cell wall actively pumps ions into the vacuole.
The vacuole lacks a surrounding membrane.
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the membrane surrounding the vacuole. It facilitates the transport of several ions and other materials into the vacuole against their concentration gradients.

questions.question_text: Which combination is present in the mitochondrial matrix?
options: Circular DNA, RNA molecules, 70S ribosomes and components for protein synthesis
questions.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix contains a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, 70S ribosomes and the components required for protein synthesis.

questions.question_text: A chromosome has its centromere close to one end, producing one extremely short arm and one very long arm. How is this chromosome classified?
questions.explanation: An acrocentric chromosome has its centromere close to one end, producing one extremely short arm and one very long arm. A telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life' For NEET Test 4

questions.question_text: How are phospholipids arranged in the plasma membrane?
options: The hydrophobic tails face the aqueous environment on both sides of the membrane.
The polar heads face the outer sides, while the hydrophobic tails remain towards the inner part of the bilayer.
The polar heads and hydrophobic tails are arranged randomly throughout the membrane.
The polar heads remain buried within the membrane, while the tails face the outer sides.
questions.explanation: Phospholipids form a bilayer in which the polar heads face the outer aqueous sides and the hydrophobic tails remain towards the inner part. This protects the non-polar tails from the aqueous environment.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes peripheral membrane proteins from integral membrane proteins?
options: Peripheral proteins are made only of lipids, whereas integral proteins are made only of carbohydrates.
Peripheral proteins occur only in prokaryotic cells, whereas integral proteins occur only in eukaryotic cells.
Peripheral proteins are buried in the bilayer, whereas integral proteins lie only on its surface.
Peripheral proteins lie on the membrane surface, whereas integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.
questions.explanation: Membrane proteins are classified according to their ease of extraction. Peripheral proteins lie on the membrane surface, while integral proteins are partially or completely buried within the membrane.

questions.question_text: A neutral solute moves across the plasma membrane from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration without using energy. Which process is involved?
questions.explanation: Neutral solutes may cross the plasma membrane by simple diffusion along their concentration gradient, from higher to lower concentration. This is a form of passive transport and does not require energy.

questions.question_text: Which prokaryotic organism is an exception to the general presence of a cell wall outside the plasma membrane?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes generally possess a cell wall surrounding the plasma membrane, but Mycoplasma is an exception and lacks a cell wall.

questions.question_text: Which sequence lists the three parts of a bacterial flagellum?
options: Axoneme, radial spoke and basal body
questions.explanation: A bacterial flagellum consists of a filament, hook and basal body. The filament is its longest portion and extends from the cell surface to the outside.

questions.question_text: Which pair of subunits forms a 70S ribosome?
questions.explanation: A 70S ribosome consists of a larger 50S subunit and a smaller 30S subunit. Prokaryotic ribosomes and the ribosomes within mitochondria and chloroplasts are 70S.

questions.question_text: Which combination correctly describes lysosomes?
options: Non-membrane-bound structures containing enzymes active at alkaline pH
Double-membrane-bound structures containing enzymes for ATP synthesis
Membrane-bound vesicles containing hydrolytic enzymes optimally active at acidic pH
Flattened sacs containing chlorophyll pigments and circular DNA
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes. These enzymes are optimally active at acidic pH and can digest carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

questions.question_text: A cell is actively synthesising lipids and lipid-like steroidal hormones. Which organelle is expected to be particularly well developed?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site of lipid synthesis. In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are also synthesised in the SER.

questions.question_text: What is the principal role of the contractile vacuole in Amoeba?
questions.explanation: The contractile vacuole of Amoeba is important for osmoregulation and excretion. Food vacuoles, in contrast, are formed by engulfing food particles.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly describes the cytoskeleton?
options: A membrane-bound system composed of cisternae, tubules and vesicles
A rigid cellulose layer that protects the plasma membrane
A network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments involved in support, motility and maintenance of cell shape
A collection of hydrolytic enzymes enclosed within acidic vesicles
questions.explanation: The cytoskeleton is an elaborate network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments in the cytoplasm. It provides mechanical support and contributes to motility and maintenance of cell shape.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life Chapter-Wise Test 5

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly explains the fluidity of the plasma membrane in the fluid mosaic model?
options: Carbohydrates move freely through the hydrophobic interior of the membrane.
The quasi-fluid nature of lipids permits the lateral movement of proteins within the bilayer.
Membrane proteins remain permanently fixed between two rigid lipid layers.
Phospholipids form a rigid layer that prevents movement of membrane components.
questions.explanation: In the fluid mosaic model, the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer allows proteins to move laterally within it. This movement is measured as membrane fluidity and is important in processes such as secretion, endocytosis and cell division.

questions.question_text: Which process describes the movement of water across the plasma membrane by diffusion?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water by diffusion across the plasma membrane. It is a passive process and does not require the expenditure of cellular energy.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the formation of the secondary wall in a plant cell?
options: It is formed on the inner side of the primary wall as the cell matures.
It is formed outside the middle lamella in a young, actively growing cell.
It replaces the plasma membrane when the cell stops growing.
It is formed only between two neighbouring plant cells.
questions.explanation: The primary wall of a young plant cell is capable of growth. As the cell matures, this capacity gradually decreases and the secondary wall is formed on the inner side, towards the plasma membrane.

questions.question_text: Which pathway correctly represents the movement of materials through the Golgi apparatus?
options: Trans face → cisternae → cis face → endoplasmic reticulum
Cisternae → endoplasmic reticulum → cis face → trans face
Endoplasmic reticulum → cis face → Golgi cisternae → trans face
Endoplasmic reticulum → trans face → cis face → Golgi cisternae
questions.explanation: Vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis or forming face of the Golgi apparatus. Materials move through the cisternae and are released from the trans or maturing face.

questions.question_text: Which combination of structures is characteristic of a typical plant cell but absent from an animal cell?
options: Cell wall, plastids and a large central vacuole
Nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation: Plant cells possess a cell wall, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent from animal cells. Animal cells possess centrioles, which are absent from almost all plant cells.

questions.question_text: A bacterium has a comma-shaped cell. Which basic bacterial form does it represent?
questions.explanation: Vibrio is the comma-shaped bacterial form. Bacillus is rod-like, coccus is spherical and spirillum is spiral in shape.

questions.question_text: Which pair of subunits constitutes an 80S ribosome?
questions.explanation: An 80S ribosome consists of a larger 60S subunit and a smaller 40S subunit. Cytoplasmic ribosomes of eukaryotic cells are 80S.

questions.question_text: Where are chlorophyll pigments located within a chloroplast?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids. The thylakoids occur in the stroma and may be arranged into stacks called grana.

questions.question_text: A chromosome possesses a non-staining secondary constriction at a constant location. What appearance may this produce?
questions.explanation: A non-staining secondary constriction at a constant location may give the appearance of a small chromosome fragment called a satellite.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes microbodies?
options: They are non-membrane-bound granules found only in prokaryotic cells.
They are double-membrane-bound organelles containing 70S ribosomes.
They are cylindrical structures that form spindle fibres in animal cells.
They are minute membrane-bound vesicles containing various enzymes in plant and animal cells.
questions.explanation: Microbodies are minute membrane-bound vesicles that contain various enzymes. They occur in both plant and animal cells.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life Chapter-Wise Test 6

questions.question_text: Which of the following is identified as the largest isolated single cell?
questions.explanation: The egg of an ostrich is the largest isolated single cell. Nerve cells are among the longest cells, while human red blood cells are approximately 7.0 µm in diameter.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly gives the approximate composition of the plasma membrane of a human erythrocyte?
options: 40 per cent protein and 52 per cent lipid
52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipid
52 per cent carbohydrate and 40 per cent protein
40 per cent carbohydrate and 52 per cent lipid
questions.explanation: The membrane of a human erythrocyte contains approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipid. The protein-to-lipid ratio varies considerably among different cell types.

questions.question_text: Why do polar molecules generally require carrier proteins to cross the plasma membrane?
options: They are too small to enter the membrane.
They can move only against their concentration gradient.
They are repelled by the polar heads of phospholipids.
They cannot pass readily through the non-polar lipid bilayer.
questions.explanation: Polar molecules cannot pass readily through the non-polar interior of the lipid bilayer. They therefore require membrane carrier proteins to facilitate their movement across the plasma membrane.

questions.question_text: What is the principal role of plasmodesmata in plant tissues?
options: They connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.
They attach chromosomes to spindle fibres.
They connect the thylakoids of different grana.
They join the inner and outer mitochondrial membranes.
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata traverse the cell walls and middle lamellae of neighbouring plant cells. They establish connections between the cytoplasm of adjacent cells.

questions.question_text: The Golgi apparatus is an important site for the formation of which substances?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies materials received from the endoplasmic reticulum and is an important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

questions.question_text: Approximately how much of the volume of a plant cell may be occupied by vacuoles?
questions.explanation: Vacuoles may occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of a plant cell. A vacuole is a membrane-bound cytoplasmic space enclosed by the tonoplast.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly compares the number of chloroplasts in Chlamydomonas and a mesophyll cell?
options: Both normally contain one chloroplast per cell.
Chlamydomonas contains 20–40 chloroplasts, whereas a mesophyll cell contains one.
Both normally contain 20–40 chloroplasts per cell.
Chlamydomonas may contain one chloroplast, whereas a mesophyll cell may contain 20–40.
questions.explanation: The number of chloroplasts varies among cells. Chlamydomonas may have one chloroplast per cell, whereas a mesophyll cell may contain approximately 20–40 chloroplasts.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes cilia from flagella?
options: Cilia are relatively short and may move the cell or surrounding fluid, whereas flagella are longer and are responsible for cell movement.
Cilia contain microtubules, whereas flagella contain only microfilaments.
Cilia are not covered by the plasma membrane, whereas flagella are membrane-bound.
Cilia occur only in prokaryotes, whereas flagella occur only in eukaryotes.
questions.explanation: Cilia are comparatively short and work like oars, moving either the cell or the surrounding fluid. Flagella are longer and are mainly responsible for movement of the cell.

questions.question_text: What is the perinuclear space?
options: The space enclosed within the nucleolus
The 10–50 nm space between the two membranes of the nuclear envelope
The space between the nucleus and the endoplasmic reticulum
The space occupied by chromatin during cell division
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel membranes separated by a space of approximately 10–50 nm. This intervening region is called the perinuclear space.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between the centromere and kinetochores?
options: The kinetochore joins two chromosomes, while the centromere forms the satellite.
The centromere occurs only in interphase, whereas kinetochores occur in the nucleolus.
The centromere is the primary constriction that holds two chromatids, and kinetochores occur on its sides.
The centromere is a secondary constriction formed between two kinetochores.
questions.explanation: The centromere is the primary constriction of a chromosome and holds its two chromatids together. Disc-shaped structures called kinetochores are present on the sides of the centromere.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life Chapter-Wise Test 7

questions.question_text: The endoplasmic reticulum divides the intracellular space into which two compartments?
questions.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum divides the intracellular space into a luminal compartment within the ER and an extra-luminal compartment represented by the cytoplasm.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly identifies the shapes of the two faces of the Golgi apparatus?
options: Both the cis and trans faces are convex.
The cis face is concave, whereas the trans face is convex.
Both the cis and trans faces are concave.
The cis face is convex, whereas the trans face is concave.
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus has a distinct convex cis or forming face and a concave trans or maturing face. The two faces are different but interconnected.

questions.question_text: Gas vacuoles are found in which group of prokaryotes?
options: Blue-green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria
questions.explanation: Gas vacuoles occur in blue-green bacteria and in purple and green photosynthetic bacteria. They are distinct from the non-membrane-bound granules that store reserve materials.

questions.question_text: Which description correctly represents the internal organisation of a centriole?
options: Nine peripheral doublets surrounding two central microtubules
Eight peripheral triplets surrounding a membrane-bound hub
Nine peripheral triplets connected to a central hub by radial spokes
Nine peripheral singlets surrounding two central tubules
questions.explanation: A centriole has nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils, each composed of a microtubule triplet. A proteinaceous central hub is connected to the peripheral triplets by radial spokes.

questions.question_text: Which pair consists of mature cells that may lack a nucleus?
options: Erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve-tube cells of vascular plants
Human cheek cells and onion epidermal cells
Nerve cells and columnar epithelial cells
questions.explanation: Some mature cells lack a nucleus. Examples include erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve-tube cells of vascular plants.

questions.question_text: What does the letter “S” in 70S and 80S ribosomes represent?
options: The Svedberg unit of sedimentation coefficient
questions.explanation: “S” represents the Svedberg unit or sedimentation coefficient. It is indirectly related to the density and size of a ribosomal particle.

questions.question_text: Which combination is present in the stroma of a chloroplast?
options: Enzymes for carbohydrate and protein synthesis, circular DNA and ribosomes
Cristae, mitochondrial DNA and respiratory enzymes
questions.explanation: The chloroplast stroma contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. It also contains small double-stranded circular DNA molecules and ribosomes.

questions.question_text: What primarily determines the number of mitochondria present in a cell?
options: The thickness of the plasma membrane
The physiological activity of the cell
The number of chromosomes in the cell
questions.explanation: The number of mitochondria varies among cells according to their physiological activity. Mitochondria also show considerable variation in shape and size.

questions.question_text: Which combination may occur in the cell wall of algae?
options: Cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals such as calcium carbonate
questions.explanation: Algal cell walls may contain cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals such as calcium carbonate. In other plants, the wall contains cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins and proteins.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes chromoplasts?
options: They contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments that may impart yellow, orange or red colour.
They are colourless plastids specialised only for protein storage.
They contain no pigments but possess large quantities of starch.
They contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest cellular macromolecules.
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls. These pigments may give plant parts a yellow, orange or red colour.

tests.title: Cell: The Unit of Life Chapter-Wise Test 8

questions.question_text: Which observation was made by Matthias Schleiden after examining a large number of plants?
options: New cells arise only through the division of pre-existing cells.
Animal cells possess a thin outer layer called the plasma membrane.
Plants are composed of different kinds of cells that form their tissues.
The nucleus contains material that can be stained by basic dyes.
questions.explanation: Matthias Schleiden examined many plants and concluded that they are composed of different kinds of cells that form plant tissues. He and Theodore Schwann later formulated the cell theory.

questions.question_text: Which hypothesis was proposed by Theodore Schwann from his studies of animal cells and plant tissues?
options: The bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.
All cells contain a cell wall outside the plasma membrane.
Chromosomes become visible only after the nuclear envelope disappears.
questions.explanation: Schwann proposed that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells. His work with Schleiden formed the basis of the cell theory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a stated function of the plant cell wall?
options: Protecting the cell from mechanical damage and infection
Providing a barrier to undesirable macromolecules
Controlling the movement of RNA and proteins between the nucleus and cytoplasm
questions.explanation: The cell wall gives shape, protects against mechanical damage and infection, assists cell-to-cell interaction and restricts undesirable macromolecules. Movement between the nucleus and cytoplasm occurs through nuclear pores.

questions.question_text: Which description correctly represents the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus?
options: Spherical vesicles, each approximately 5–10 µm in diameter
Flat, disc-shaped sacs approximately 0.5–1.0 µm in diameter, stacked parallel to one another
Tubular structures arranged as nine peripheral microtubule triplets
Membranous sacs arranged into stacks called grana
questions.explanation: Golgi cisternae are flat, disc-shaped sacs approximately 0.5–1.0 µm in diameter. A variable number of cisternae are stacked parallel to one another and arranged near the nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the multiplication of mitochondria?
options: Mitochondria arise by packaging within the Golgi apparatus.
Mitochondria form by fusion of lysosomal vesicles.
Mitochondria are produced from the nuclear envelope.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria divide by fission. They also possess circular DNA, RNA, 70S ribosomes and components needed for the synthesis of some proteins.

questions.question_text: Plastids are stated to occur in which organisms?
options: Only the mesophyll cells of higher plants
questions.explanation: Plastids occur in plant cells and euglenoids. On the basis of pigments and stored material, they are classified as chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.
