questions.question_text: Why are scientific names preferred over local names?
options: Scientific names are always shorter than local names.
They provide a universally accepted name for each organism.
Local names cannot be used for plants.
They indicate the complete evolutionary history of an organism.
questions.explanation: Local names vary from place to place. Scientific nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same name throughout the world, avoiding confusion.

questions.question_text: What does “Linn.” indicate in the biological name Mangifera indica Linn.?
options: The plant belongs to the family Linnaceae.
The plant was first discovered in India.
The generic name has been abbreviated.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.
questions.explanation: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

questions.question_text: Which category contains organisms with the greatest number of common characteristics?
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest category among the given options. Members of lower taxa share more common characteristics than members of higher taxa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: Only the economic uses of organisms
Only the external appearance of organisms
Only the habitats occupied by organisms
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes systematics?
options: It is limited only to classification.
It deals only with assigning scientific names.
It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It excludes the study of relationships among organisms.
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about binomial nomenclature is incorrect?
options: A biological name has two components.
The generic name always begins with a small letter.
Biological names are written in italics when printed.
The system was given by Carolus Linnaeus.
questions.explanation: The generic name begins with a capital letter, whereas the specific epithet begins with a small letter. Both words are written in italics when printed.

questions.question_text: What is meant by identification in the study of living organisms?
options: Grouping organisms only according to their uses
Assigning different local names to the same organism
Placing every organism directly in a kingdom
Determining the organism to which a particular name is attached
questions.explanation: Identification involves correctly describing an organism and determining the organism to which a particular name is attached.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes classification?
options: It groups organisms into convenient categories based on observable characters.
It has no role in the study of biological diversity.
It is based only on the economic importance of organisms.
questions.explanation: Classification is the process of grouping organisms into convenient categories based on easily observable characters, making their study manageable.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the language of biological names is correct?
options: Biological names must be written in the local language.
Only plant names are written in Latin.
Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised, irrespective of their origin.
The generic name and specific epithet must come from different languages.
questions.explanation: Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised irrespective of their origin. When printed, they are written in italics.

questions.question_text: Which category is used in plant classification in place of phylum?
questions.explanation: In plants, classes with a few similar characters are assigned to the higher category called division. The corresponding category in animals is phylum.

questions.question_text: On what basis were the earliest classifications of organisms made?
options: Their positions in the taxonomic hierarchy
questions.explanation: The earliest classifications were based on the uses of organisms because human beings needed sources of food, clothing and shelter.

questions.question_text: What does “Linn.” indicate in the biological name Mangifera indica Linn.?
options: The plant belongs to the family Linnaceae.
The plant was first found in India.
The generic name has been abbreviated.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.
questions.explanation: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

questions.question_text: What does the term “taxon” represent in biological classification?
options: A unit of classification representing a rank or category
A rule used for writing scientific names
A group based only on the uses of organisms
questions.explanation: A taxon is a unit of classification representing a rank or category. Species, genus, family and order are taxa at different levels of the hierarchy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly represents the taxonomic hierarchy in descending order?
options: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Species → Genus → Family → Order → Phylum → Class → Kingdom
Kingdom → Phylum → Family → Order → Class → Genus → Species
questions.explanation: The descending hierarchy in animals is Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species. In plants, division is used in place of phylum.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes a species?
options: It is a group of related genera.
It is the highest category of classification.
It is a group of organisms occupying the same habitat.
It is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
questions.explanation: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. One species can be distinguished from a closely related species by distinct morphological differences.

questions.question_text: Panthera and Felis are placed together in Felidae. What does this demonstrate?
options: A genus contains several related families.
A family contains related genera with some common characteristics.
An order contains only one genus.
A species contains several unrelated genera.
questions.explanation: A family is a group of related genera. Felidae includes the related genera Panthera and Felis .

questions.question_text: Who gave the system of binomial nomenclature described in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus gave the system of binomial nomenclature, in which each biological name has a generic name and a specific epithet.

questions.question_text: Felidae and Canidae are placed together in which higher taxonomic category?
questions.explanation: Felidae and Canidae are related families included in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families sharing a few similar characters.

questions.question_text: What is the taxonomic status of Panthera tigris ?
options: It is the biological name of a species.
questions.explanation: Panthera tigris is the biological name of the tiger species. Panthera is the generic name, while tigris is the specific epithet.

questions.question_text: Which combination of information forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: Only the economic uses and local names of organisms
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
Only the reproductive structures of plants
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: Why is standardised scientific nomenclature necessary?
options: It ensures that a particular organism is known by the same name throughout the world.
It permits every region to assign a different scientific name.
It eliminates the need to identify an organism.
It restricts biological names to economically useful organisms.
questions.explanation: Local names vary from place to place. Standardised nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same scientific name throughout the world.

questions.question_text: An organism is moved from its species category towards its kingdom. Which change is expected?
options: The number of shared characteristics increases.
The number of included organisms decreases.
The number of shared characteristics decreases.
questions.explanation: As one moves from species towards kingdom, categories become broader and the number of common characteristics shared by their members decreases.

questions.question_text: Why is classification necessary for studying living organisms?
options: It assigns names without describing organisms.
It groups organisms into convenient categories because studying all organisms individually is nearly impossible.
It restricts biological study to familiar organisms.
It groups organisms only according to their economic uses.
questions.explanation: Because it is nearly impossible to study all living organisms individually, classification groups them into convenient categories and makes their study manageable.

questions.question_text: A student identifies an organism as wheat. Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents wheat?
options: Genus: Mangifera ; Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Sapindales
Genus: Musca ; Family: Muscidae; Order: Diptera
Genus: Triticum ; Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Poales
Genus: Triticum ; Family: Poaceae; Order: Poales
questions.explanation: Wheat is Triticum aestivum . It belongs to the genus Triticum , family Poaceae and order Poales.

questions.question_text: An investigator first groups organisms into convenient categories and then assigns scientific names after identifying them. Which conclusion is correct?
options: These processes are components of taxonomy.
These processes are unrelated to taxonomy.
questions.explanation: Classification, identification and nomenclature are basic processes of taxonomy. Characterisation is also included in taxonomic studies.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about nomenclature is correct?
options: Each organism may have several accepted scientific names.
Scientific nomenclature ensures that an organism is known by the same name throughout the world.
Scientific names change with the local language of a region.
Nomenclature can be completed without correctly describing the organism.
questions.explanation: Standardised nomenclature ensures that a particular organism is known by the same scientific name throughout the world, avoiding confusion caused by different local names.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about systematics is correct?
options: It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It is restricted to the assignment of scientific names.
It does not consider relationships among organisms.
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: Which taxonomic rank is the lowest category that can include organisms belonging to different genera but sharing common characteristics?
questions.explanation: A family is a group of related genera. For example, the genera Panthera and Felis are included in the family Felidae.

questions.question_text: Potato, brinjal and black nightshade have the specific epithets tuberosum , melongena and nigrum , respectively. What can be inferred from the chapter?
options: All three belong to the same species.
All three belong to the family Felidae.
Each belongs to a different kingdom.
All three belong to the genus Solanum .
questions.explanation: Solanum includes species with specific epithets such as tuberosum , melongena and nigrum . They are different species belonging to the same genus.

questions.question_text: A human is classified under Hominidae and Mammalia. Which category lies between these two ranks?
questions.explanation: Hominidae is the family, Primata is the order and Mammalia is the class of humans. Therefore, Primata lies between Hominidae and Mammalia.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the handwritten form of a biological name?
options: The generic name and specific epithet are underlined separately.
Only the generic name is underlined.
Both words are enclosed within quotation marks.
The two words are joined and underlined as one unit.
questions.explanation: When a biological name is handwritten, the generic name and specific epithet are underlined separately. When printed, both words are written in italics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following taxonomic categories contains organisms with the fewest common characteristics?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the highest and broadest category among the given options. As one moves from species towards kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN)?
options: It provides principles for assigning scientific names only to plants.
It provides internationally accepted principles for the scientific naming of animals.
It permits the same scientific name to be assigned to different known animals.
It replaces the binomial system of nomenclature in animals.
questions.explanation: The ICZN provides internationally accepted principles for assigning scientific names to animals. Such naming procedures help ensure that each organism has a distinct scientific name.

questions.question_text: Which taxonomic category includes the fewest organisms among the following?
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest and most specific category among the given options. Lower categories include fewer organisms whose members share more characteristics.

questions.question_text: A human is placed in the family Hominidae and the class Mammalia. Which category lies between these two ranks?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the family Hominidae, order Primata and class Mammalia. Therefore, Primata lies between Hominidae and Mammalia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scientific names is written correctly?
questions.explanation: In a printed biological name, the generic name begins with a capital letter, the specific epithet begins with a small letter, and both words are italicised: Panthera tigris .

questions.question_text: Panthera and Felis are grouped together in Felidae. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Felidae is an order containing related families.
Felidae is a family containing related genera.
Felidae is a genus containing related species.
Felidae is a class containing related orders.
questions.explanation: A family contains related genera. The genera Panthera and Felis are included in the family Felidae.

questions.question_text: Which combination forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: Only economic uses and local names
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: What does “Linn.” indicate in the biological name Mangifera indica Linn.?
options: The plant belongs to the family Linnaceae.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.
The specific epithet has been abbreviated.
The plant was first identified in India.
questions.explanation: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet identifies the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes systematics from a study limited to nomenclature?
options: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also considers evolutionary relationships.
Systematics is limited only to assigning scientific names.
Systematics considers only the economic uses of organisms.
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents wheat?
options: Genus: Mangifera ; Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Sapindales
Genus: Triticum ; Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Poales
Genus: Triticum ; Family: Poaceae; Order: Poales
Genus: Musca ; Family: Muscidae; Order: Diptera
questions.explanation: Wheat is Triticum aestivum . It belongs to the genus Triticum , family Poaceae and order Poales.

questions.question_text: Who used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word systema .

questions.question_text: Which international code provides agreed principles and criteria for the scientific naming of plants?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
questions.explanation: The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature provides agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants.

questions.question_text: Which combination of information forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: Only the external appearance of organisms
Only the economic uses and local names of organisms
Only the habitat and geographical distribution of organisms
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly explains the term “taxon”?
options: It refers only to the species category.
It is a rule for writing biological names.
It is a unit of classification representing a rank or category.
It refers only to groups of animals.
questions.explanation: A taxon is a unit of classification representing a rank or category. Species, genus, family and class are taxa at different hierarchical levels.

questions.question_text: What is meant by identification in the study of living organisms?
options: Grouping organisms only according to their uses
Assigning several local names to the same organism
Placing an organism in a kingdom without describing it
Determining the organism to which a particular name is attached
questions.explanation: Identification involves correctly describing an organism and determining the organism to which a particular name is attached.

questions.question_text: Which statement about species is correct?
options: A species is an assemblage of related genera.
A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
Every species belongs to several different genera.
Closely related species cannot be distinguished morphologically.
questions.explanation: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. Closely related species can be distinguished from one another by distinct morphological differences.

questions.question_text: Felidae and Canidae share a few similar characters and are placed together in which category?
questions.explanation: Felidae and Canidae are related families placed in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families sharing a few similar characters.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the scope of systematics?
options: It deals only with assigning names to organisms.
It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It groups organisms only according to their economic uses.
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between phylum and class in animal classification?
options: A class contains several related phyla.
Class and phylum represent the same rank.
questions.explanation: Related classes are grouped into a phylum in animal classification. For example, classes containing fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are included in Chordata.

questions.question_text: A human is classified under the genus Homo and the order Primata. Which category lies between these two ranks?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the genus Homo , family Hominidae and order Primata. Therefore, Hominidae lies between the genus and order.

questions.question_text: Solanum tuberosum , Solanum melongena and Solanum nigrum illustrate which taxonomic principle?
options: A family contains only one species.
A specific epithet can be used without a generic name.
All organisms in a genus have the same specific epithet.
A genus may include several related species.
questions.explanation: The genus Solanum includes several related species with different specific epithets, such as tuberosum , melongena and nigrum .

questions.question_text: Which international code provides agreed principles and criteria for the scientific naming of plants?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
questions.explanation: The International Code for Botanical Nomenclature provides agreed principles and criteria for assigning scientific names to plants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about classification is incorrect?
options: It groups organisms into convenient categories.
It may use easily observable characters for grouping organisms.
It makes the study of the large diversity of organisms manageable.
It is applicable only to animals and not to plants.
questions.explanation: Classification applies to all organisms, including plants and animals. It groups organisms into convenient categories and makes their study manageable.

questions.question_text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents mango?
options: Genus: Triticum ; Family: Poaceae; Order: Poales
Genus: Mangifera ; Family: Solanaceae; Order: Polymoniales
Genus: Mangifera ; Family: Anacardiaceae; Order: Sapindales
Genus: Musca ; Family: Muscidae; Order: Diptera
questions.explanation: Mango is Mangifera indica . It belongs to the genus Mangifera , family Anacardiaceae and order Sapindales.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly represents the taxonomic hierarchy from lowest to highest?
options: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom
Genus → Species → Family → Order → Phylum → Class → Kingdom
Species → Family → Genus → Class → Order → Phylum → Kingdom
Order → Family → Genus → Class → Species → Phylum → Kingdom
questions.explanation: The ascending hierarchy in animals is Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom. In plants, division is used in place of phylum.

questions.question_text: Felidae and Canidae share a few similar characters. In which higher category are these families placed together?
questions.explanation: Felidae and Canidae are related families included in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families that share a few similar characters.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a rule of biological nomenclature?
options: Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised.
The first word represents the genus and the second denotes the specific epithet.
The two words are underlined separately when handwritten.
The generic name begins with a small letter.
questions.explanation: The generic name begins with a capital letter, whereas the specific epithet begins with a small letter. When handwritten, the two words are underlined separately.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes systematics?
options: It is restricted to assigning scientific names.
It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and considers evolutionary relationships.
It classifies organisms only according to their economic uses.
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification. It also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: Which of the following taxonomic categories is the most specific?
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest and most specific taxonomic category. Its members share more characteristics than members grouped at higher taxonomic levels.

questions.question_text: On what basis were the earliest classifications of organisms made?
options: Their positions in the taxonomic hierarchy
questions.explanation: The earliest classifications were based on the uses of organisms because human beings needed sources of food, clothing and shelter.

questions.question_text: Which option correctly represents the taxonomic position of humans as given in the chapter?
options: Homo sapiens , Felidae, Primata, Mammalia, Chordata
Homo sapiens , Hominidae, Carnivora, Mammalia, Chordata
Homo sapiens , Canidae, Carnivora, Mammalia, Chordata
Homo sapiens , Hominidae, Primata, Mammalia, Chordata
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the species Homo sapiens , family Hominidae, order Primata, class Mammalia and phylum Chordata.

questions.question_text: Which international code provides principles for the scientific naming of animals?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
questions.explanation: The International Code of Zoological Nomenclature provides internationally accepted principles for assigning scientific names to animals.

questions.question_text: An organism is considered successively at the species, genus, family and kingdom levels. Which change is expected as one moves towards kingdom?
options: The number of shared characteristics increases.
The difficulty of determining relationships decreases.
The number of shared characteristics decreases.
questions.explanation: As one moves from species towards kingdom, the categories become broader and the number of common characteristics decreases. Determining relationships among taxa at higher levels also becomes more difficult.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the taxonomic hierarchy is incorrect?
options: Species is the lowest taxonomic category.
Kingdom is the highest category described in the hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Order is placed below class and above family. The ascending sequence is species, genus, family, order, class, phylum or division, and kingdom.

questions.question_text: Which combination of taxonomic categories correctly represents the housefly?
options: Genus: Musca ; Family: Felidae; Order: Carnivora
Genus: Musca ; Family: Muscidae; Order: Diptera
Genus: Homo ; Family: Hominidae; Order: Primata
Genus: Triticum ; Family: Poaceae; Order: Poales
questions.explanation: The housefly is Musca domestica . It belongs to the genus Musca , family Muscidae and order Diptera.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes a species?
options: It is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities.
It is an assemblage of several related genera.
It is a group of organisms occupying the same habitat.
It is the highest category in the taxonomic hierarchy.
questions.explanation: A species is a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities. Closely related species can be distinguished from one another by distinct morphological differences.

questions.question_text: Panthera leo , Panthera pardus and Panthera tigris illustrate which taxonomic principle?
options: A species may contain several unrelated genera.
A family always contains only one genus.
All organisms in a genus have the same specific epithet.
A genus may contain several closely related species.
questions.explanation: The genus Panthera includes closely related species such as lion, leopard and tiger, represented by the specific epithets leo , pardus and tigris .

questions.question_text: Which combination of features is mentioned for animals placed in phylum Chordata?
options: Three pairs of jointed legs and an external skeleton
A notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system
External ears and body hair only
questions.explanation: Animals such as fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are placed in Chordata based on common features such as a notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system.

questions.question_text: On what basis were the earliest classifications of organisms made?
options: Their positions in the taxonomic hierarchy
questions.explanation: The earliest classifications were based on the uses of organisms because human beings required sources of food, clothing and shelter.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about binomial nomenclature is incorrect?
options: A biological name has two components.
The specific epithet is written before the generic name.
Biological names are generally in Latin or are Latinised.
The system was given by Carolus Linnaeus.
questions.explanation: The generic name is written first and is followed by the specific epithet. For example, in Mangifera indica , Mangifera is the generic name and indica is the specific epithet.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about systematics is incorrect?
options: Its scope includes identification, nomenclature and classification.
It takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.
It is restricted only to naming and classifying organisms.
The word systematics is derived from the Latin word systema .
questions.explanation: Systematics is not restricted to naming and classification. It includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also considers evolutionary relationships among organisms.

questions.question_text: Which combination forms the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: Only local names and economic uses
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: A plant is placed in a category above class and below kingdom. Which category should be used?
questions.explanation: In plants, classes with a few similar characters are grouped into a division. Division corresponds to phylum in animal classification.

questions.question_text: A taxonomist moves from the species rank towards kingdom while classifying an organism. Which combination of changes is expected?
options: Categories become narrower and common characteristics increase.
Categories become narrower and relationships become easier to determine.
Common characteristics increase and fewer organisms are included.
Categories become broader and common characteristics decrease.
questions.explanation: As one moves from species towards kingdom, categories become broader and include more organisms, while the number of common characteristics decreases. Relationships at higher ranks are also more difficult to determine.

questions.question_text: A student places humans in Hominidae and Chordata. Which pair of categories must occur between these two ranks?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the family Hominidae, order Primata, class Mammalia and phylum Chordata. Therefore, Primata and Mammalia occur between Hominidae and Chordata.

questions.question_text: A tiger and a lion belong to Panthera , while a domestic cat belongs to Felis . Which conclusion is correct?
options: The tiger and lion share more characteristics with each other than either shares with the cat.
All three belong to the same genus because they are in Felidae.
The domestic cat belongs to the genus Panthera .
The tiger and lion belong to different families.
questions.explanation: The tiger and lion belong to the same genus, Panthera , whereas the cat belongs to Felis . Members of the same genus share more characteristics than members placed only in the same family.

questions.question_text: A specimen is identified as Mangifera indica . Which additional classification is correct?
questions.explanation: Mangifera indica is mango. It belongs to the family Anacardiaceae and the order Sapindales.

questions.question_text: A biologist assigns a scientific name to an organism before establishing which organism the name represents. Which essential step has been omitted?
options: Identification through correct description of the organism
questions.explanation: Nomenclature is possible only when the organism is correctly described and the organism to which the name is attached is known. This process is identification.

questions.question_text: Two animal families, Felidae and Canidae, share a few similar characters. At which rank are they grouped together?
questions.explanation: Felidae and Canidae are related families included in the order Carnivora. An order is an assemblage of families that share a few similar characters.

questions.question_text: Early humans grouped certain organisms together because they supplied food, clothing or shelter. Which basis of classification does this illustrate?
options: Classification based on the uses of organisms
Classification based on taxonomic hierarchy alone
questions.explanation: The earliest classifications were based on the usefulness of organisms to humans, especially as sources of food, clothing and shelter.

questions.question_text: A student analyses the name Solanum tuberosum . Which interpretation is incorrect?
options: The two words together form the biological name of potato.
tuberosum alone is the complete scientific name of the species.
questions.explanation: A complete binomial name contains both the generic name and the specific epithet. Therefore, tuberosum alone is not the complete biological name; the correct name is Solanum tuberosum .

questions.question_text: A researcher identifies organisms, assigns scientific names, classifies them and studies their evolutionary relationships. Which field best describes this work?
questions.explanation: Systematics includes identification, nomenclature and classification and also takes evolutionary relationships among organisms into account.

questions.question_text: A student writes the biological name of mango by hand as Mangifera indica , underlining both words together with a single line. Which correction is required?
options: Both words should begin with capital letters.
The generic name and specific epithet should be underlined separately.
The specific epithet should be written before the generic name.
Only the specific epithet should be underlined.
questions.explanation: When a biological name is handwritten, the generic name and specific epithet are underlined separately. The generic name begins with a capital letter, while the specific epithet begins with a small letter.

questions.question_text: A taxonomist is comparing four newly identified organisms. Which set of information should be used for a modern taxonomic study?
options: Only their external colour and size
Only their habitats and local names
Only their economic uses and geographical locations
External and internal structure, cell structure, development and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies use external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes and ecological information.

questions.question_text: A human is placed in the genus Homo and the class Mammalia. Which pair of categories occurs between these two ranks?
questions.explanation: Humans belong to the genus Homo , family Hominidae, order Primata and class Mammalia. Therefore, Hominidae and Primata occur between genus and class.

questions.question_text: Two organisms are placed in the same species, while another pair is placed only in the same genus. Which pair is expected to share more characteristics?

The pair placed only in the same genus
Both pairs must share exactly the same number of characteristics
The relationship cannot be inferred from taxonomic rank
questions.explanation: Species is a lower and more specific category than genus. Members of lower taxa share more characteristics than members grouped at higher taxonomic levels.

questions.question_text: A label reads Mangifera indica Linn. What can be concluded from “Linn.”?

The plant was first collected in India.
The generic name has been abbreviated.
The species was first described by Linnaeus.
questions.explanation: The abbreviated author name written after the specific epithet indicates the scientist who first described the species. “Linn.” indicates Linnaeus.

questions.question_text: A taxonomist groups the families Felidae and Canidae together because they share a few similar characters. Which taxonomic category has been formed?
